clue.text: Worthy — linen draper-poor horseman

parts.note: describes the hero of Cowper's comic ballad, a respectable London citizen and draper whose borrowed horse bolts with him all the way to Ware

explanation.surface: A character sketch: a decent shopkeeper who is hopeless in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: William Cowper's 1782 ballad tells of a 'citizen of credit and renown', a linen draper, whose runaway ride is the joke of the poem; knowing the poem is the only way in.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballad's title character is a worthy draper whose ride on a borrowed horse goes comically wrong.

clue.text: Refuses to supply, sails

definitions.meaning: a horse that refuses a fence stops short; to balk

explanation.surface: Someone declines to provide the canvas for a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To balk at something is one sense; the triangular headsails of a yacht are the other.

clue.text: Workman's pass

definitions.meaning: a manual worker, as in farm worker or deckhand
to pass something over to someone

explanation.surface: A labourer's permit to get through.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm or factory worker is one sense; to give or pass over is the other.

clue.text: Potter's method throwing one on the other side

definitions.text: Potter's method throwing one on the other side

parts.words: Potter's method throwing one on the other side
parts.note: Stephen Potter's book on the art of winning games by unsettling the opponent; 'throwing' suggests a potter's wheel

explanation.surface: A potter's technique for throwing clay on the far side of the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: The potter is not a craftsman at the wheel but Stephen Potter, who wrote a 1947 book on putting the other side off its game.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsettling an opponent by legal but sly tricks, the art Stephen Potter wrote about.

clue.text: Money Man, for instance what a yarn!

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for the pound, from Latin libra
the Isle of Man is an example of an island

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a tall tale about a rich man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' looks like a tall story, but it is thread: lisle is a fine, hard-twisted cotton thread used for stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a smooth cotton thread, originally from the French town of Lille.

clue.text: Ernest's in trouble for doing nothing

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters are in disarray and must be put in a new order

parts.note: the name Ernest with its 's, counting the S

explanation.surface: A man called Ernest gets into difficulty for being idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is part of the fodder and 'trouble' the signal: ERNEST, S and IN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertness is a state of inactivity, of not moving or acting.

clue.text: Put the dagger in (would be crazy to turn it)

indicators.note: the bracket says that turning the answer round would give a word meaning crazy, so read it backwards

parts.note: bats is informal for crazy, mad

explanation.surface: An instruction to stab, with a parenthetical warning that undoing it would be madness.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket works backwards from the answer: 'to turn it' means writing it the other way round gives BATS, slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a dagger into someone is to strike with a pointed blade, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Old pulpit in Italian city noted by maker of jingles

indicators.note: in puts the old pulpit inside the city's name

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy
an ambo is a raised reading desk in early churches
E is a musical note, added at the end

explanation.surface: An ancient pulpit in Turin, remarked upon by a percussionist.
explanation.walkthrough: An AMBO was an early Christian pulpit. 'Noted' adds a note, E. 'Jingles' looks like advertising tunes but means the little metal discs on the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The tambourine has small metal discs round its frame that jingle when shaken.

clue.text: Top wines this author is said to provide

parts.note: best means top, finest

indicators.note: is said marks a word that sounds like the one we want

parts.note: a cellar is a store of wines

explanation.surface: A writer is said to supply the finest wines.
explanation.walkthrough: A wine collection is called a cellar, which sounds like SELLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of a book that sells in huge numbers is called this, by extension from the book.

clue.text: Alexander, such a noted leader

parts.note: Irving Berlin's song Alexander's Ragtime Band calls him 'the leader of the band'; 'noted' hints at musical notes as well as fame

explanation.surface: Alexander the Great hailed as a famous commander.
explanation.walkthrough: The name points to Alexander the Great, but the song Alexander's Ragtime Band makes him a leader of musicians; 'noted' is the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A conductor of a brass or military band is its leader, the man in front of the players.

clue.text: A 'medicine-man's also a prophet

parts.note: MO, the medical officer, is a medicine man; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A tribal healer who also turns out to foretell the future.
explanation.walkthrough: MO stands for Medical Officer, an army doctor. The 's on 'medicine-man's' supplies the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Nazi fighter in attack on transport vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the attack word above the vessel

parts.note: to storm is to attack
a trooper is a troopship, a vessel for carrying soldiers

explanation.surface: A German soldier taking part in an assault on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link. A TROOPER is a ship carrying troops; 'on' stacks STORM above it in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sturmabteilung, the Nazi party's paramilitary, were known in English by this name.

clue.text: Oriental outstations can be so flamboyant

indicators.note: the letters of the words that follow can be rearranged into something new

parts.note: E, for East, stands for oriental

explanation.surface: Remote outposts in the East are prone to showiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can be' signals the anagram: E (East, for 'Oriental') plus OUTSTATIONS is rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy and fond of display, a close synonym of flashy or flamboyant.

clue.text: Defective hot-water bottle makes one gloomy

definitions.text: Defective hot-water bottle makes one gloomy

parts.words: Defective hot-water bottle makes one gloomy
parts.note: a leaking bottle would soak the bedclothes; the soaked bedding is also the name for a killjoy

explanation.surface: A leaking hot-water bottle puts you in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: A leaky bottle leaves soaked bedding, and the phrase for that is also a person who dampens everyone's fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport who dampens enthusiasm is called this, after smothering a fire with damp cloth.

clue.text: Dreamy Athenian 'tailor with a lean and hungry look ?

definitions.meaning: Robin ..., the tailor among the Athenian workmen in A Midsummer Night's Dream

definitions.text: with a lean and hungry look ?

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean tailor looking thin and underfed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tailor in A Midsummer Night's Dream bears the name, and it also means an underfed, emaciated person.

clue.text: Send abroad for trial of super sort of diet

parts.note: extra means super, outstanding, as in extra fine

indicators.note: sort here works as a verb, to sort or rearrange the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a superb new diet is being shipped abroad to be tested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' looks like a test of the diet, but it is part of the definition: sending someone to another country to face a court. 'Sort of' rearranges DIET into DITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand a suspect over to another country's courts is the legal process of surrender.

clue.text: Just put Section One into mail sorting

indicators.note: into puts the section and the one inside the sorted mail
sorting puts the letters of mail in a new order

parts.note: a part is a section
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An instruction to put Section One into the post being sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only', but here it is the adjective meaning fair. 'Sorting' is the anagram signal and 'into' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fair and unbiased is what impartial means.

clue.text: Such rides as Cobbett enjoyed

parts.note: refers to William Cobbett's book ... Rides, accounts of his horseback tours of the English countryside

explanation.surface: A question about the outings a historical figure liked.
explanation.walkthrough: William Cobbett, an English radical writer, published Rural Rides (1830) about riding through farming country; the answer is the first word of that title.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobbett's journeys were through the countryside, so they were of the country and farmland.

clue.text: Robert is ardent

definitions.meaning: to be on fire with passion, a verb in the third person

explanation.surface: A man named Robert is passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish poet's surname, and a verb for blazing with feeling.

clue.text: Numbers stick around, reporting history in this

indicators.note: around means the word for stick wraps about the numbers

parts.note: to paste is to stick, glue
tens are numbers

explanation.surface: Sums of figures plus an adhesive, then an account of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' signals the container. The definition works because narrated history and reported speech both use the verb form for completed actions.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts of history and reported speech use the verb form for completed past actions.

clue.text: One speech after well-cooked meal."That's. an improvement

indicators.note: after places the speech and the one behind the cooked meal
cooked means messed about with, so the letters of meal are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: An after-dinner speech that follows a good meal makes things better.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an after-dinner speech; 'well-cooked' is the anagram signal and 'after' places the speech behind the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelioration is the act of making something better, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Traffic exit from 15

indicators.note: from tells you to remove the exit letters from the answer to 15

parts.note: the answer to 15 across
the letters of exit, removed in order

explanation.surface: Looks like a road sign for leaving the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: Take E, X, I and T, in that order, out of EXTRADITE (15 across) and TRADE is left. 'Traffic' means dealing in goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic in the sense of commerce, buying and selling, is a synonym.

clue.text: My customary refusal to comply?

definitions.meaning: an old word for habitual, as in 'as is my habit'
will not, said by someone refusing

explanation.surface: A person whose usual response is to refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Wont means habitual, as in 'as he was wont to do'; with an apostrophe, it is the contraction of will not.

clue.text: Love is absolutely cold

explanation.surface: A romantic claim that love is utterly frigid.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is nothing in tennis scoring, and the lowest possible temperature is absolute nothing on the scale.

clue.text: Join-a needlework class to do so?

definitions.meaning: to unite, as broken bones do when they mend

definitions.text: a needlework class to do so?
definitions.meaning: a class in needlework might teach you to make garments with needles and yarn

explanation.surface: A suggestion to sign up for a sewing class, and do what is taught there.
explanation.definitionFit: Bones mending together is a sense of the word, and so is working yarn with needles.

clue.text: Ovid paper's difficult-take a dim view

indicators.note: difficult suggests the words are in a troublesome state, mixed up into a new order

parts.note: the Roman poet's name, used as written
the word paper with its 's giving a final S

explanation.surface: A Latin poet's essay is hard going, so a reader frowns on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult' tells you to rearrange OVID and PAPERS (the 's counts) into ten new letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something unfavourably is the same idea as to frown on or object to it.

clue.text: Show, attachment to state in classical style

definitions.text: Show, attachment to state in classical style

parts.words: Show, attachment to state in classical style
parts.note: describes the Roman citizen's garment, worn to show belonging to the state; on a second look 'to' attached to a US state abbreviation spells it

explanation.surface: Displaying patriotism in an old-fashioned, classical way.
explanation.walkthrough: Only Roman citizens could wear this robe, so putting it on showed loyalty to the state; TO joined to GA (Georgia) makes the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The draped woollen robe was the formal dress of a citizen of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Give the bird to everyone for a start, fairly briskly

indicators.note: for a start puts the word for everyone at the front of the answer

parts.note: all means everyone
an egret is a kind of heron, a bird

explanation.surface: An instruction to boo everyone at the outset, done at a fair clip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give the bird' looks like jeering, but the bird is EGRET; 'for a start' puts ALL first. Allegretto is a musical tempo marking, a little slower than allegro.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian tempo marking asks for a fairly quick pace, a little slower than allegro.
